clue.text: Sensible mother taking time away from routine

indicators.note: one thing taking another holds it, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for mother
T is the abbreviation for time
off means away, as in 'off on holiday'
a comedian's routine is an act
joins the last piece on

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth mum takes a break from the daily grind.
explanation.walkthrough: Mater is old public-school slang for mother. 'Routine' feels like part of the break from the grind, but it is a stage turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter-of-fact person is practical and unemotional, which is what sensible means here.

clue.text: Top scorer I see score at Christmas

parts.note: Lionel Messi, the footballer famed as a prolific goalscorer
'Ah!' is what you say when you see the point

explanation.surface: A football star appears to be watching a game played on Christmas Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' of the surface is part of the phrase 'I see', not a letter on its own; the score is a musical one, not a football result.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's oratorio Messiah is a musical score traditionally performed in the Christmas season.

clue.text: Jazz means improvised sparks, perhaps

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

indicators.note: something improvised is made up on the spot, so these letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Improvised jazz is the way to strike sparks of creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparks is British slang for an electrician, a typical skilled tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrician, nicknamed sparks, is one example of a skilled manual worker; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Attractive topless picture offered suggestively

indicators.note: without its top, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: fetching means attractive

explanation.surface: A saucy topless photo is being shown off with a wink.
explanation.walkthrough: FETCHING loses its F. The definition alludes to the old line 'Come up and see my etchings', a famously suggestive invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from an etched plate, the picture a seducer proverbially invites someone up to see.

clue.text: Enthusiasm raised low bar

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word turns it to read bottom to top

parts.note: a cow lows, that is, moos
PH, public house, is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: Spirits are lifted in a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb for what cattle do, not the opposite of high.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for energy and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Become less wrinkly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to suit, as a dress becomes someone
second meaning: more smooth and even, comparative of an adjective

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single instruction, to smooth out, but 'Become' is a verb meaning to suit and the rest is a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment that flatters you suits you, and a surface with fewer creases is more level, the comparative sense.

clue.text: Fish to be paid for at the door?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the common food fish

definitions.text: to be paid for at the door?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the initials of cash on delivery

explanation.walkthrough: Cash on delivery means paying the courier when the parcel reaches your door; the question mark marks the playful paraphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The cod is a familiar sea fish, and the abbreviation describes goods paid for on arrival at home.

clue.text: African's visit blocked by northeast winds

indicators.note: a passage blocked by something has that thing lodged inside it, so pieces go within another

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
NE is the abbreviation for northeast
gales are strong winds

explanation.surface: A traveller's trip is held up by bad weather from the northeast.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion falls after the second letter rather than in the middle, which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Senegal in West Africa is Senegalese; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Entertaining woman shows not all marriage is happy

indicators.note: the phrase displays only part of the words that follow, so the entry is inside them

parts.note: found across the end of one word, the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A wise woman observes that not every marriage is a happy one.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain guests with conversation, music and dance.

clue.text: Soldier cage fighting punches American flat

indicators.note: punching goes through into something, so one piece is driven inside the other

parts.note: a condo, short for condominium, is the American term for an owned apartment
MMA, mixed martial arts, is fought in a cage

explanation.surface: A cage fighter goes through the wall of an American apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an adjective describing the punches, but it is the noun for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier in an elite raiding unit.

clue.text: Two small pieces of fruit for auditor's vitamin deficiency

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the phrase concerns what is heard rather than written

parts.note: two berries said one after the other

explanation.surface: An accountant snacking on a couple of berries hopes to fend off scurvy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' tempts you towards accounts, but it simply means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is the disease caused by a lack of vitamin B1, thiamine.

clue.text: Container with two lids?

parts.note: surface reading: a pot or jar with a double cover
setter's reading: lid is slang for a hat, so this box holds one lid and is closed by another

explanation.walkthrough: Lid is informal for headgear; a box made for headgear has its own lid on top and a second inside.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a case designed for storing and carrying a hat, itself fitted with a cover.

clue.text: Moving pre-divorce not worth it

indicators.note: things that are moving get shifted about, so these letters change places

parts.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Relocating before the divorce comes through isn't worth the cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs more than its value, so it is not worth the money.

clue.text: Bath perhaps is no longer hot

parts.note: what is no longer the case once was
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the bath water has gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the English spa city at the head of the clue, but it is the everyday tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is one kind of wash, a session of cleaning oneself; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Empty manhole opening behind Charlie, a long way

indicators.note: an emptied word has its insides removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only
an opening is a gap
British slang for the backside
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An open manhole cover lies some distance behind a man called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as a preposition but is a noun for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaparsec is a million parsecs, an astronomical unit of distance of over three million light years.

clue.text: Swans crossing river, son out of bread

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, so one piece sits across the others

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
the Nile, Africa's great river
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Swans flying over a river leave a son without any bread to feed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son out of' reads like the son is removed, but 'out of bread' is the definition; bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To be penniless is to have no money, and bread is informal for cash.

clue.text: Rich area wants horrible stink gone by November

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so these letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Wealthy residents want an awful smell gone by November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just adds N to the anagram fodder. Kensington is an affluent district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington is a wealthy part of London, known for grand houses and museums.

clue.text: It's like carpaccio, Italian agreed, eating a thin strip

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: si is Italian for yes
A plus SHIM, a thin slip of material used to pack a gap

explanation.surface: An Italian diner agrees to order a raw beef starter, taking a thin slice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is thinly sliced raw fish, just as carpaccio is thinly sliced raw meat or fish.

clue.text: Premier with dress, what we remember May for?

parts.note: premier means first or top
gear is clothing

explanation.surface: Theresa May, the Prime Minister, was noted for her outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: Premier and May point to Theresa May, but the definition means James May, a presenter of the BBC motoring show.
explanation.definitionFit: James May is best known for co-presenting the BBC car programme, so that show is his claim to fame.

clue.text: Utensil for wiping yard down

parts.note: a mop is used to wipe floors
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Someone is told to mop the yard, working downward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' sounds like a direction for mopping, but it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means low-spirited, and mopy describes someone listless and gloomy.

clue.text: Heavy weather made of first day at work before long

parts.note: Monday, abbreviated, starts the working week
soon means before long

explanation.surface: Someone makes heavy weather of their first day in a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make heavy weather of' is an idiom for struggling, but here 'Heavy weather' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A monsoon is a season of very heavy rain in South Asia.

clue.text: Traitor with relaxed manner heading for lunch

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
ease is a relaxed, unhurried manner

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A double-crosser strolls off casually to lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is informal for a sly, treacherous person who betrays others.

clue.text: Fast finish for concerto's slow movement

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A concerto ends quickly after its slow movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, the opposite of the answer, but it is the noun for a period of abstaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the tempo marking for a slow pace, and a movement so marked is a slow one.

clue.text: Louvre architect designed Ringo's dressing gown

parts.note: I. M. Pei designed the glass pyramid at the Louvre

indicators.note: a design is a new arrangement, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous architect turned his hand to a robe for Ringo Starr.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a woman's light dressing gown or negligee.

clue.text: Cool at one, change clothes

indicators.note: clothing wraps around a body, so one piece is put around the others

parts.note: small change is pence
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone cool at one o'clock changes into other clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' and 'clothes' look like a verb and its object, but change is coins and clothes is the verb meaning to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool as a noun means composure, as in keeping one's cool, which is close to patience.

clue.text: American shot past

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a shot at something is a go

explanation.surface: An American gunman fired a shot in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, earlier than now.

clue.text: Travelling bride perhaps on top of the world heading west

indicators.note: in an across entry, west is leftward, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: re means on, concerning
the North Pole is at the top of the globe

explanation.surface: A newlywed on honeymoon feels on top of the world as she heads west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top of the world' reads as one happy phrase, but 'on' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride who runs away to marry in secret is an eloper; 'perhaps' notes she is one example.

clue.text: Beloved writer isn't in room or elsewhere

indicators.note: letters put elsewhere are moved out of position, making a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A much-loved author is not in her study but somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beloved' looks like praise, but it is the title of her 1987 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Toni Morrison, the Nobel-winning American novelist, wrote the novel Beloved.
